death.note: Died on the night of Tuesday, 22nd of Jumādā al-Ūlā, 806 H. He was buried the next morning.

relation.note: Served as the junior dawādār for Sultan al-Nāṣir (Faraj b. Barqūq, wd:Q698037; reigned 801–815 H, consistent with the subject's death in 806 H). Upon his death, al-Nāṣir seized his inheritance. Corrected the hallucinated wd:Q192809 to wd:Q698037.

event.desc: Left a considerable inheritance, including, it is said, twelve thousand gold dinars, which Sultan al-Nāṣir seized.
event.note: Occurred upon his death in 806 H.
Reported by al-Badr al-ʿAynī (Pattern A third-party mention).

person.note: アクブガー・アル＝ジュンディーは、ナーシル（スルタン）の小ダワーダール（副ダワーダール）を務めた法学者（ファキーフ）であった。 806年ジュマーダー・アル＝ウーラー月22日火曜日の夜に死去し、翌日埋葬された。 彼は多くの遺産を残したが、言い伝えによれば現金の金貨1万2千ディナールも含まれており、これをナーシルが受け取った。 彼は職務において評価されておらず、むしろ賄賂や汚職、公金横領、禁じられた行為に手を染めたことで知られていたと、アル＝アイニーが語っている。

Aqbaghā al-Jundī, the faqīh and junior dawādār for al-Nāṣir. He died on the night of Tuesday, the 22nd of Jumādā al-Ūlā, in the year 806 H, and was buried the next morning. He left a substantial estate, including, it is said, twelve thousand gold dinars in cash, which al-Nāṣir subsequently seized. He was not commended in his official capacity; rather, he was known for bribery, corruption, embezzlement of funds, and engaging in forbidden acts, as reported by al-ʿAynī.
